The study used a genetic algorithm (GA) to optimize the turbine performance.
The design variables considered in this study are the stagger, inlet, and outlet angles of the blades.
The objective function used in this study is polytropic efficiency.
The optimization process resulted in an improvement of 8.4% in torque.
The optimization process resulted in an improvement of 0.69% in power.
The optimization process resulted in an improvement of 1.2% in polytropic efficiency.
The computational domain used in this study is a three-dimensional model of the turbine blades.
The mesh used in this study is an unstructured tetrahedral and prismatic element mesh.
The rotational speed considered in this study is 8000, 6400, 4800, and 3200 rev/min.
The turbine exit static pressure was varied from 9 to 3 bars at different pressure ratios.
The study used a SIMPLE scheme to couple the velocity pressure.
The study used a high-resolution second-order scheme to discretize the advection term.
The study used a core i7 (12 core) CPU operating at a speed of 4 GHz.
The study used a grid with 4,501,103 cells.
The study considered 15 Prism layers, a growth rate of 1.4, and an initial layer thickness of 10^-3 mm.
